batch: Classify six works from complete open documents and authoritative publisher or institutional records
policy: These are work-scope judgments only. They do not certify complete object extraction, endorse readings, resolve identities or authenticity, or change text and media rights.

entries.basis: The complete volume prints Ellis's transcriptions reduced to Hebrew or Syriac characters, with translations and philological remarks, for a numbered series of Babylonian bowls (Nos. 1-6 are separately headed and a further fragment group is summarised). It edits many objects rather than studying a theme. The series total is reported differently by later scholarship and is not settled here.

The complete chapter states that the new material the author can present 'is limited to a single text' and confines itself to one Nippur bowl from the University of Pennsylvania collection, published separately by permission of Hilprecht and Montgomery ahead of Montgomery's corpus volume.

The complete article edits one vase newly entered into the Cabinet des Antiques of the Bibliotheque Nationale, giving its physical description, the transcription of its two spiral inscriptions, a translation and a commentary, and closing on the client Hisda son of Ama.

The Bar-Ilan institutional record states that the volume gives editions of sixty-four Jewish Aramaic incantation bowls from the Schoyen Collection with introductions, translations, philological notes, photographs and indices, as the first instalment of a multi-volume corpus publication.

The publisher's description states that the book prints the texts of all legible Aramaic amulets then known together with thirteen hitherto unpublished bowls, each supplied with translation and commentary and supported by a detailed glossary. It edits many objects.

The University of California Press description frames the book as a comparative study of rabbinic identity and authority in the Sasanian context, drawing on Middle Persian Zoroastrian literature, seals, inscriptions and the Aramaic bowl spells as evidence alongside the Talmud. It is a sustained thematic argument, not an object edition.
